script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for June 12. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Athletes run faster in races than in practice.  Students try harder when competing for grades.  Countries push harder in rivalries.

Research shows we perform better against specific rivals than against the field. Having a named competitor raises our game more than abstract goals. Rivals become measuring sticks that push us beyond what we'd achieve alone. Competition becomes destructive when winning matters more than improving.  Cheating, sabotage, and crushing opponents aren't competitive benefits—they're competitive failures.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Opposition can be a gift.  Competition teaches that challenges reveal and develop our capabilities.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Healthy Rivalry - Find Your Competition.

Here's your activity: Identify a healthy rival—someone whose progress challenges you to improve. Not someone to beat or destroy, but someone who raises your game. Or compete with yourself: track performance and try to beat yesterday's record. This helps you use competition constructively.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about why we compete can be applied to healthy rivalry - find your competition. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
